content.comment_body: Hello, I created a simple control for an output in [product_name]. I assigned animated icons from the library to reflect the on/off status. When connected through LAN, the icons display properly. However, when I access the system remotely over mobile 4G using a DNS host, the icons do not appear, although I can still operate the output. Am I missing something?

Hi, It sounds like your [product_name] project works on the local network, but not when you connect through 4G; the graphics are missing in that case. This likely means your browser is unable to load the visual assets remotely. There is a known issue with certain communication modules not properly delivering web graphics when accessed from outside your network. As a workaround, you might try using the [product_name] based message text web server through 4G instead. Is this issue only present on mobile phones or tablets, or does it also happen if you access with a PC through 4G? Try clearing your browser cache, loading the page locally first, then reconnecting via 4G; this may allow the graphics to display from your cached files instead of remotely. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: The main user experience issue is that icons configured in a [product_name] project display correctly over a local LAN connection, but do not appear when accessed remotely via 4G and DNS host. Device controls still function, indicating only the graphics are affected. A reply explains this is a common remote access issue with certain [product_name] communication modules, recommends caching strategies or alternative connectivity methods, and confirms the limitation is graphical rather than functional.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects all icons and visual features in the web interface to work seamlessly and display correctly both locally and when accessing the system remotely, not just within the local network.
